editorial_changes: Proposition 1.4.1 now displays the domain inequalities, conjugate-denominator calculation, both inverse compositions, quotient-rule derivatives, metric substitution and perpendicular-coordinate area scaling.

A new paragraph substitutes the full fractional k(theta) action into C and factors both numerator and denominator, displaying the geometric angle 2 theta. The geodesic proof displays the transformed circle/line equation.
Proposition 1.4.3 retains the full arguments of d_H and u throughout, and defines the domains of z,w,g,zeta,eta explicitly.
The disk formula is proved by directly subtracting the two inverse Cayley fractions and dividing by the product of their imaginary parts.
The orbit proof defines the diagonal action, separates same-orbit implies equal-invariant from its converse, handles radius zero, and exhibits g₂⁻¹kg₁ sending both entries to their targets.
The invariant-function conclusion explains surjectivity onto every t≥0 and why a unique common value defines h(t).
Proposition 1.4.4 derives rho=tanh(r/2) using r=d_H(i,w) and the two preceding expressions for u(i,w), then computes the polar metric and area and the ball-area integral.

The radial integral starts with the nonnegative Tonelli case, separates angular factor 2 pi from substitution factor 2, and proves the complex case after absolute integrability. The zero-area polar center and the geometric-angle convention are stated.
All five semantic labels and numbers 1.4.1–1.4.5 are retained. The notation index has 66 rows, distinguishing disk radius rho from the elliptic vertex rho.
Recorded the explicit-function-arguments convention in AGENTS.md for later editing rounds; any shorter symbol must first be defined locally.
